note: Past events and forward expectations from the AI monitoring fleet. FOUR ROW TYPES, deliberately not merged: 'observed' are dated facts with a source; 'model-expect' are numbered consequences a model ASSERTS (no probability — the kinds do not produce one); 'expert-claim' are dated claims by named commentators, registered before resolution with criteria we wrote, not theirs; 'joint-claim' are brainstorm synthesis claims and are the ONLY rows carrying a number — an LLM panel's confidence, not a calibrated forecast. Every future row is a WINDOW (start..end), not a point: 'by <date>' means any time up to that date. NOTHING IS GRADED — every future row is open.

**By 2027-12-31, at least one significant divergence will be documented between leaderboard rank and independently-assessed task performance.** Absence over the window supports the orthodoxy and counts hard against this model.

**By 2027-12-31, at least one study will separate AI substitution from offshoring in the same occupations.** Until C3 is separated, this attribution is incomplete and should be stated as such rather than asserted.

**By 2027-12-31, at least two further frontier releases will carry cyber-specific access restrictions or defender-only variants.** Absence falsifies P2.
**By 2027-12-31, at least two major AI training-data disputes will resolve by settlement rather than merits judgment.** Two merits rulings instead violate P3.
**By 2027-12-31, commentator prominence (citations, bookings) will show no measurable relationship to resolved accuracy.** A positive relationship falsifies P1 — and would be good news.

**By 2027-12-31, continual learning will remain unsolved** — no frontier model shipped with persistent cross-session learning as a headline capability. Shipping one falsifies P3 and is the strongest single indicator this timeline is wrong.

timeline.item: **By 2027-12-31, if US-China talks produce any AI-specific agreement, actors sorted RHETORICAL will shift to a different justification** rather than accepting the constraint. Accepting it falsifies the sort.

**By 2027-12-31, no Chinese firm will publicly announce a large purchase of US-origin frontier accelerators under the case-by-case pathway.** An announcement violates P4 — and would say the pathway is working as trade policy rather than as a control.
**By 2027-12-31, no US court will enjoin the operation of a frontier model product.** An injunction violates P4 and is the single highest-impact event this model watches.
**By 2027-12-31, no US court will hold a frontier model developer liable for a deployer's downstream use.** Such a holding violates P2 and would redraw where risk sits in the whole industry.

**By 2027-12-31, no federal statute imposing binding pre-deployment obligations on frontier model developers will be enacted.** Enactment violates P1 and is the single most informative event for this model.

**By 2027-12-31, no frontier lab will publicly demonstrate a model autonomously producing a capability improvement that the lab attributes primarily to the model rather than to its researchers.** A clean demonstration resolves this against the model.

**By 2027-12-31, no frontier release will demonstrate a capability discontinuity attributable to pretraining scale alone**, separable from post-training and inference-time compute. A clean demonstration defeats this model — and that is the outcome it must accept.

**By 2027-12-31, no leading Chinese lab will publicly attribute a halted or abandoned frontier training run to accelerator unavailability.** Such an attribution violates P2 and would mean export controls bind harder than modelled.
**By 2027-12-31, the Aug 2026 transparency rules will NOT have caused any frontier lab to alter a product beyond adding disclosure text.** A substantive product change falsifies the P2 sort.
**Export-control changes will be written in terms of tool and chip specifications, not model capabilities, through 2027-12-31.** A control written against model capability instead falsifies P4.
**For at least two US federal AI instruments issued before 2027-12-31, step-4 language will be traceable to a step-2 document published earlier.** Failure on both falsifies P1 and most of this model.

**No more than half of entities that become consequential by 2027-12-31 will have been absent from the ledger.** A miss rate above half falsifies the method — this is the consequence that can actually kill the model.
timeline.model_title: Power Centres Before They Are Obvious

timeline.item: **Through 2027-12-31, AI-attributed revenue at the top five will keep growing year-over-year**, even if decelerating. Contraction defeats this model.
**Through 2027-12-31, US and UK aggregate unemployment will not show a discontinuity attributable to AI.** A discontinuity would mean P1 was wrong and the aggregate frame missed the event.
timeline.model_title: What Actually Moved the Job Numbers

timeline.item: **Through 2027-12-31, aggregate hyperscaler capex will not fall more than 30% year-over-year.** A fall that steep defeats this model.

**Through 2027-12-31, announced datacentre completions will lag their interconnection applications by more than 24 months on average**, where both dates are public. Falsified if the typical gap is under 24 months.

**Through 2027-12-31, at least 70 percent of decisions taken by actors in `options/` will be options this model enumerated in advance.** Below 70 percent means the enumeration method fails - the most important single number here.
**Through 2027-12-31, each publicly documented AI-enabled attack technique will precede a widely deployed defence against it by at least 6 months.** Falsified if defence ships first, twice.
**Through 2027-12-31, measured net-negative shifts in AI sentiment polling will precede new state AI enactments in the same jurisdiction by 12-24 months.** Falsified if enactments lead sentiment.
**Through 2027-12-31, no forced-sale or distressed-financing event will occur at a major AI infrastructure operator.** Such an event is the leverage mechanism P1 says is absent.

**Through 2027-12-31, no frontier training run will be publicly delayed for reasons traceable to lithography capacity** — the lag is long enough that today's constraint has not yet bitten. A delay attributed to it falsifies the claimed lag length.
**Through 2027-12-31, no top-five hyperscaler will take an AI-infrastructure impairment charge exceeding 10% of its AI asset base.** A larger charge supports the bubble thesis directly.
**Through 2027-12-31, taken options will be EVIDENCED more often than UNEVIDENCED, across at least 10 graded decisions.** Parity or worse kills P3 and the awareness layer with it.

**Through 2027-12-31, the junior/senior employment gap in AI-exposed occupations will persist or widen, while remaining absent in non-AI-exposed occupations.** If the same gap appears in non-exposed occupations, C2/C4 explain it and this attribution fails.
timeline.model_title: What Actually Moved the Job Numbers

timeline.item: **US state laws sorted SYMBOLIC under P3 will not produce a material product change through 2027-12-31.** A change falsifies the sort — and would mean private-right-of-action is not the discriminating feature.

By 2027-12-31, reporting will confirm Anthropic and/or OpenAI's compute-capacity growth was substantially financed via off-balance-sheet leases/SPVs rather than retained earnings, even if operating profit is independently real.
timeline.criteria: TRUE if credible reporting (10-K equivalent, S-1, investigative financial press) shows majority of incremental compute capacity financed off-balance-sheet; FALSE if shown predominantly self-funded from retained earnings/cash flow.

timeline.item: Jim VandeHei: "There's very little data that AI is destroying tons of jobs in real time"
timeline.criteria: Corroborate against ai-labor-attribution's aggregate evidence; consistent with that model's P1 as of 2026-09.

timeline.item: John Schulman: "even if the model can write way more code than a person, it doesn't make you 100X more productive"
timeline.criteria: Through 2027-12-31, does any frontier lab publish a credible claim of >=10x AI research productivity? Directly opposes Amodei's RSI timeline.

timeline.item: Matt Sheehan: "China's major AI policy documents take a diffuse approach to compute, prioritising applications over consolidation"
timeline.criteria: Through 2027-12-31, does China announce consolidation of frontier compute behind a single national champion lab? If yes, Sheehan's read fails.

timeline.item: Matt Sheehan: "the race-to-takeoff model doesn't have the chokehold in China that it does in the US"
timeline.criteria: By 2027-12-31, do official Chinese AI policy documents adopt explicit takeoff/AGI-race framing?

timeline.item: Richard Campbell: "we're headed down the trough of disillusionment just fine, far from bottomed out, but on our way down"
timeline.criteria: By 2027-12-31: has AI investment sentiment measurably declined from the 2026-06 level (funding volume, valuations, or a >25% drawdown in AI-linked equities)? See ai-bubble-thesis consequence 1.

timeline.item: Dylan Patel: "by the end of next year half of the incremental compute is already going to Anthropic and OpenAI"
timeline.criteria: By 2027-12-31, do credible estimates place OpenAI+Anthropic at >=45% of incremental compute additions?

timeline.item: Dwarkesh Patel: "You could not keep a four-month gap between internal and external deployment and still be competitive"
timeline.criteria: By 2028-08-07: does the median internal-to-public deployment gap at frontier labs fall below one month, where observable?

timeline.item: Dwarkesh Patel: "continual learning will create a clear moat for the leading AI labs that they currently lack"
timeline.criteria: By 2028-08-07, conditional on continual learning shipping: do enterprise switching rates between frontier providers fall measurably vs 2026 baseline?

timeline.item: Dwarkesh Patel: "pre-deployment evaluation will not be a meaningfully distinct category in the future"
timeline.criteria: By 2028-08-07: has any major regulator shifted from pre-deployment gating to periodic provider inspection, citing continuous model updating?

timeline.item: Dwarkesh Patel: "the diversity of AI minds will increase"
timeline.criteria: By 2028-08-07: do instances of the same base model demonstrably diverge in behaviour based on deployment history, as documented by the provider?

timeline.item: Jim VandeHei: "If we keep doing what we're doing, you're going to end up with China winning the AI war or the rich getting richer"
timeline.criteria: By 2028-08-26, has any national AI coordinating framework of the kind described been established in the US?

timeline.item: Dario Amodei: "interpretability improvements possible in 1-2 years with focused effort"
timeline.criteria: By 2028-09-12, has a frontier lab published interpretability results it characterises as enabling reliable detection of deceptive or misaligned behaviour in a deployed frontier model?

timeline.item: Dwarkesh Patel: "it's just really wild for me to consider that the margins for something like intelligence will be greater than 90% and they don't get competed away"
timeline.criteria: By 2028-12-31, do reported frontier inference gross margins exceed 90% on a sustained basis?

timeline.item: Dwarkesh Patel: "smarter AI models could drive up compute prices 10x"
timeline.criteria: By 2028-12-31, is the frontier-grade compute price per GPU-hour at least 5x the February 2026 spot trough? (10x is the headline; 5x is the generous test.)

timeline.item: Dylan Patel: "We're at a little bit over a trillion dollars of CapEx this year. As we go out into '28, it's going to be more than $2 trillion"
timeline.criteria: Does reported aggregate AI capex for 2028 exceed $2T, per two independent published estimates?

timeline.item: Dario Amodei: "3-5 year window to execute chip restrictions before AI becomes geopolitically most important"
timeline.criteria: By 2029-09-12, is the US-China frontier compute gap wider, narrower, or unchanged vs 2026-09-12 baseline (est. China at 1/8 to 1/10 of US)?
